headlines.text: Looking back to 2026, when it was title-change night for the AEW World Trios Titles as Brodido & Page vs. The Demand battled it out, appearing on Grand Slam: Mexico, rated 7.53 ? a match that delivered ? ending the champion's reign at 2 defenses. It was the first title opportunity of Brodido & Page's career. It was the 60th time the AEW World Trios Titles had been on the line, a real piece of championship history. "Hangman" Page, Bandido and Brody King ? "The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly" ? dethroned The Demand for the AEW World Trios Championship at Grand Slam Mexico.

Looking back to 2020, when Jon Moxley vs. Darby Allin clashed for the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.08 ? a real highlight of the night. A tough title defense for Moxley against the rising young star, on a night that also saw the Dark Order's full stable of eight overwhelm The Elite and FTR in the opener.

Looking back to 2022, when Josh Woods went straight to headlining on debut in a Street Fight match, appearing on Rampage, rated 7.25 ? a well-worked match. Woods made his AEW in-ring impact alongside Tony Nese in a Friday Night Street Fight against the tag champions, highlighted by a twisting brainbuster into the ring steps.

secondaries.text: Rewind to 2023, when FTR vs. Bill & Cage clashed for the AEW World Tag Team Titles, appearing on Collision, rated 7.40 ? a match that delivered. It was the first title opportunity of Bill & Cage's career.

Rewind to 2026, when Kyle Fletcher vs. Mike Bailey clashed for the AEW International Title, appearing on Grand Slam: Mexico, rated 8.80 ? a war that left everything in the ring. Fletcher retained the AEW International Championship over Mike Bailey with a Turnbuckle Brainbuster at Grand Slam Mexico.

On a Wednesday in 2026, back when Will Ospreay vs. Mark Davis settled things in a Mexico City Street Fight match, closing out the card as the main event on Grand Slam: Mexico, rated 8.62 ? a genuine showstealer, on an outstanding Grand Slam: Mexico '26 show that earned an overall rating of 8.98. In a no-interference-allowed Mexico City Street Fight, Ospreay finally outlasted his former friend Mark Davis at Grand Slam Mexico.
